subject: Linguistics
title: Morphemes Versus Syllables
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Morphemes Versus Syllables.

hook.text: 'Elephant' has three syllables but only one morpheme—it can't be split into meaningful parts.

buildup.text: Syllables are units of sound; morphemes are units of meaning. They don't always line up.

discovery.text: '-ed' in 'walked' adds zero syllables but still adds a morpheme marking past tense.

twist.text: 'Cranberry' has two syllables for 'cran'—but 'cran' alone carries no known meaning.

climax.text: Linguists call these 'cranberry morphemes'—bound forms with no clear independent meaning.

punchline.text: Sound chunks and meaning chunks are two separate systems.
